parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
RICKY: Hi, Julie, it’s Ricky.

JULIE: Hi, Ricky, how are you? I noticed you weren’t in Psychology today.

RICKY: I’m feeling sick, so I didn’t go to school today. Would you mind telling me what I missed in class?

JULIE: Sure thing. I’m sorry you’re not feeling well! Anyway, we spent most of the class talking about a new essay that Professor Johnson assigned. You need to choose one of the bold headings from and research it.

RICKY: Wow, I picked the wrong day to miss class, huh? the note system

JULIE: You sure did.

RICKY: Could you tell me the specific requirements of this paper?

JULIE: Sure. You need to find scientific research that supports your claim as one of your references. It can be from some of the case studies we discussed in class, or you can find your own. Or even better, you can conduct your own research! I’m sure that would get you an

RICKY: Have you decided what you’re going to do yet? Also, where are you getting your references?

JULIE: Yeah, I’m going to research facial recognition by infants. I’ve already found a few experiments in scientific journals. That would probably be a good start for you - there are tons of journals in the library.

RICKY: Great idea, thanks. I’m considering writing my essay on the effects of one of the psychotropic drugs we talked about in class. I’m sure there is lots of stuff about it on the Internet. Are we allowed to use information from the Internet?

JULIE: Sure, you can use that as long as it’s not your main source for information. You’ll probably want to cite some of the experiments we went over.

RICKY: Good idea, thanks. I’m gonna try to find some information from a bunch of different sources.

RICKY: Are there any specifications on how the essay should be written?

JULIE: Yeah, Professor Johnson wants it double-spaced. It should be between 6 to 10 pages long.

RICKY: 6 to 10 pages? That’s so much! It’s going to take forever.

JULIE: I know. The whole class groaned when he said that. Anyway, you also need to put the title in italics, and...

RICKY: Wait, each section heading, or just the main heading?

JULIE: Only the main heading should be in italics. I think section titles are supposed to be in the same format, but maybe in bold. You’ll have to check that in class next time.

RICKY: Oh okay. So I take it that the report has to be typed since there are so many requirements. What are the other formatting requirements?

JULIE: Yep, it’s got to be typed. Aside from that, there are still a few more specifications. You should number each page. Make sure it goes up in the top right corner.

RICKY: Okay, I’ll make sure to write that down. I always forget to number the pages. Do we need to title and date each page, too?

JULIE: You need the shortened title on every page, but no need to include the date. That should just be on the cover page.

RICKY: Okay, thanks.

JULIE: No problem. Also, make sure the margins are 3.25 pixels wide.

RICKY: What? I’m not even sure how to do that.

JULIE: It’s okay, I can show you. It’s really easy. I think that’s all the directions he gave us. A lot of formatting requirements, but we have the freedom to research many things that we like, so that’s good. Oh, I almost forgot - remember to put down your ID number on your report.

RICKY: Thanks so much for your help. I’ll see you in class Monday!

JULIE: No problem, glad I could help. See you later.

analyses.content: Julie 告诉 Ricky 需要从 note system（笔记系统）的粗体标题中选择一个作为研究课题。
You need to choose one of the bold headings from the note system and research it.
注意听 "choose one... from the..." 后的核心名词词组，不要只填 system，要包含修饰词 note。
You need to find scientific research that supports your claim as one of your references.
题目中的 "reference" 对应原文的 "references"，所需填入的是 find 的宾语 scientific research。
Julie 指出参考文献中至少要有一项是支持观点的 scientific research（科学研究）。
I’ve already found a few experiments in scientific journals.
题目中的 "in" 是地点介词，对应原文 "found... in..."，注意 journal 需要用复数形式。
Julie 已经在 scientific journals（科学期刊）中找到了一些实验数据。
I’m sure there is lots of stuff about it on the Internet. Are we allowed to use information from the Internet?
Ricky 提到的 "lots of stuff about it on the..." 后面紧跟的就是答案，注意 Internet 首字母通常大写，也可以加 the。
Ricky 询问是否可以使用 Internet（互联网）上的信息，Julie 表示肯定。

questions.question: How should the essay be written?

analyses.content: Yeah, Professor Johnson wants it double-spaced.
不要选 C (double spaces)，那是“两个空格”的意思，而格式术语是 "double-spaced"。
Julie 明确提到教授要求文章是 double-spaced（双倍行距）的。

questions.question: The main heading is required to be

analyses.content: 关于标题格式，Julie 说只有主标题应该是 italic（斜体）的。
Only the main heading should be in italics.
不要选 C (bold)，Julie 提到小节标题（section titles）可能是粗体，但题目问的是 Main heading。

questions.question: Regarding all the requirements, the essay must be

analyses.content: Yep, it’s got to be typed.
听到 "handwritten" 的反义表达或 "typed" 的确认，排除 A。
Ricky 询问报告是否必须打印（typed），Julie 回答 "Yep, it’s got to be typed"（是的，必须打印）。

questions.question: Where should the student number the pages?

analyses.content: Make sure it goes up in the top right corner.
注意方位的听取，top（顶部）和 right（右边）缺一不可，不要选成 A（左上角）。
Julie 强调页码应该标在 top right corner（右上角）。

questions.question: What is the suitable width of the margins?

analyses.content: JULIE: No problem. Also, make sure the margins are 3.25 pixels wide.
这是一个典型的“常识陷阱”，虽然现实中“3.25像素”作为页边距极不合理（肉眼几乎不可见），但雅思听力必须遵循**“所听即所得”**原则，录音读的是 pixels，就必须选 B，严禁利用常识去选 C（centimeters）。
Julie 明确指示 Ricky 确保页边距（margins）的宽度是 3.25 pixels（3.25 像素）。

questions.question: What should be included in the essay?

analyses.content: Oh, I almost forgot - remember to put down your ID number on your report.
不要选 A（电话号码），原文明确说是 "ID number"。
Julie 最后提醒 Ricky 记得在报告上写上 ID number（学号）。
